doc.title: Benny Golson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Never expecting to see a Black President
summary: Golson never thought he would see a Black president in his time, recalling a film and television series that imagined it.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Politics, race and the state of the country

blocks.x: No, I never thought it, even though, at the end of the 18th century, there were some blacks in Congress and whatnot, but that was short-lived. That died out. No, I never thought I’d see, in my time, a black President. Although there was a film that came out with that in mind. James Earl Jones played the President. It was supposed to be a t.v. thing, and they decided to make it a theater feature. It was called The Man. I don’t know if you remember that. He was the first black American President. More recently, there was a series on, a couple of years ago, and that fellow that does the good hands with Allstate . . .
Is that his name? He was playing the President.
I think it was 24. Is that – yeah, 24 is the name of the series.
And I said, yeah, this is great fiction. Now the fiction has come to life.
Life is stranger than fiction, right?
